::: {.entry-meta}
[measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 37 · milestone M3
:::

The electron-cyclotron (EC) surrogate needs reference labels: heating and driven-current
profiles from the GENRAY ray-tracing code, for plasma states the coupling loop visits and for
the launch directions an operator would use. The [Primer](../primer.qmd) explains sources;
terms are in the [Glossary](../glossary.qmd).

**Sampling.** The plasma states come from the same family of ITER TORAX runs as transport
dataset v3: the M1 benchmark case, the ITER hybrid flat top and the ITER current ramp-up, with
heating and density scaled. The saved v3 files hold transport inputs only, so we ran the
family again and kept the electron temperature, electron density and effective charge. From
each run we take states evenly spaced in time. Each state gets launches from two launcher
families: the equatorial launcher at the upstream deck's launch point, and an upper launcher at
an approximate public position (not an ITER design value). The poloidal and toroidal angles are
drawn uniformly within each family's range. Whole TORAX runs are held out for validation and
test, so no held-out state shares a trajectory with a training state.

**Labelling.** One GENRAY process per core ran every case on one cluster node, after the owner
approved the request. Each case keeps its input deck, its output file, its logs and a record
of hashes and status. The plasma equilibrium is the same for every case: the upstream deck's
ITER file. This is the largest approximation in the dataset (ceiling [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028)). The highest
driven currents come from early ramp-up states, which are hot and dilute and in TORAX carry
only a few megaamperes, traced through an equilibrium with the full plasma current. Those
labels describe no consistent plasma. The collisional heating channel is zero in every case,
because the deck does not enable collisional damping.

| quantity | result |
|---|---|
| cases with readable output | [3120 of 3120 cases produce readable output (20 of 20 check cases); median 84.8 s of GENRAY time per case]{.claim}[C-164](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-164){.cid .st-measured} |
| current-drive method check (momentum-conserving against adjoint) | [median 4.1% difference in driven current (range -14% to +16%), identical absorbed power]{.claim}[C-165](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-165){.cid .st-measured} |
| first held-out baseline | [driven current RMSE 3.30 kA/MW against 13.5 kA/MW for the training mean; pointwise profile model: current-density RMSE 2.20e4 A/m^2 against 2.09e4 A/m^2 for the mean]{.claim}[C-166](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-166){.cid .st-measured} |

**Baseline.** We trained the existing response baseline, an unconstrained five-member
ensemble, on the totals and, separately, on the profiles point by point. The totals are
learned: the driven-current error is about a quarter of the spread of the test labels. The
pointwise profile model does no better than predicting the training mean. Deposition profiles
are narrow peaks whose position moves with the launch angle, and a model that predicts each
radius separately does not capture that. The EC surrogate therefore needs a structured
output, for example deposition centre, width and totals, the same parameters as the Gaussian
fallback.

The check of the labels is partial. GENRAY's own power and current totals agree with the
integrals of its profiles, and the two current-drive methods agree to a few per cent on the
larger currents. Neither is an independent physics validation; both use the same rays.

Next: the owner sets accuracy targets from this baseline (B3), a structured EC model is
trained (B4), and [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) is either lifted with one equilibrium per state or the ramp-up states
are restricted.
